answer: A desert trading network stays honest when every identity must answer live roll calls that arrive without warning. The first identity answers one thread of pings, the tenth juggles ten threads at once, and the twentieth faces twenty overlapping calls, each demanding a signed reply within seconds from its own key. Twenty invented agents would face 210 simultaneous summons across the epoch. Bulk farming fails because a single operator can answer only one call at a time, like a keeper who cannot draw from two shale wells and an oasis spring in the same breath.
